subject: Week 48: book the 12-month well visit — the largest vaccine round yet
bodyText:
This week
Standing alone for a few seconds is common this week, and first independent steps are emerging for some — the normal walking range is wide (9–15+ months; CDC checkpoint: 15 months: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/15-months.html). Fine motor consolidates: the pincer grasp is precise for most, and he may squat to pick up a toy and return to standing, stack two blocks, or drop objects into a container. Comprehension runs ahead of speech — expect him to follow simple gesture-plus-word directions, with first words besides mama and dada emerging for some on the same 15-month checkpoint.

Watch-fors this week
- [low concern] Frequent falls onto his bottom while cruising and standing — normal gait learning; keep hard-edged clutter off the floor.
- [monitor] No pointing, waving, or other gestures — document and raise at the 12-month visit.
- [monitor] Not pulling to stand or not bearing weight on his legs — same: document, raise at the visit.
- [call within 24h] Fever with reduced fluid intake and noticeably fewer wet diapers over a day.
- [call now] Labored breathing, blue lips, or unresponsiveness — call 911; do not second-guess.

Enrichment opportunities
- Book the first-birthday photographer this week if you want one — SF photographers book 2–4 months out, so remaining May 11 availability is already thin. Candid documentary style beats posed at this age; add a separate 15-minute everyone-in-frame slot or the cake shots will crowd it out.
- Decide the party format now and work backward: family-only (6–12 guests, 60–90 minutes, $300–800), mid-size (15–30 guests, $1,500–4,000), or venue event ($5,000+ in SF). Anchor the start time to his nap schedule — morning or early afternoon — and hold everything else to that constraint.
- Practice squat-to-pick-up: set a toy on the floor beside furniture he can hold, and let him retrieve it unassisted — the squat-and-rise transition builds the balance that precedes independent steps. AAP — movement, 8 to 12 months: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/Movement-8-to-12-Months.aspx
- Run stacking and container play daily — two soft blocks and a cup are enough. Putting an object into a container is a 12-month CDC milestone, and stacking trains the wrist control utensils will need. CDC 12-month milestones: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/1-year.html

Upcoming
- Day 364–380 (May 10–26, 2027): 12-month well visit — MMR #1, VAR #1, HepA #1, PCV #4, Hib booster, plus hemoglobin and lead screen. Book it this week; this is the largest single vaccine round of year one.
- Day 365 (Tue May 11, 2027): first birthday. Smash-cake bakery orders need 2–3 weeks of lead time; photographer availability is tighter still.
- By Day 365 (Tue May 11, 2027): first dental visit — AAP recommends by age 1 or within 6 months of the first tooth; pediatric dentists book weeks out.

Developmental milestone check-in
Tap any link to mark it complete. View or change others at https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones

- Shows you an object she likes
  AAP window: day 330-450
  What to look for: Joint attention with intention to share — distinct from pointing to request. Strong autism-screen marker when consistently absent.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/15-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/shows-object-she-likes/complete

- Follows directions given with a gesture and words
  AAP window: day 330-450
  What to look for: Combined verbal + nonverbal cues. Pure-verbal compliance comes after.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/15-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/follows-gesture-plus-words/complete

- Copies other children while playing
  AAP window: day 330-450
  What to look for: Peer-directed imitation, not just imitation of parents.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/15-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/copies-other-children/complete

- Hugs a stuffed doll or other toy
  AAP window: day 330-450
  What to look for: Pretend nurture — early symbolic play. Often emerges with a favorite lovey.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/15-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/hugs-stuffed-toy/complete

- Stacks at least two small objects (like blocks)
  AAP window: day 330-450
  What to look for: Visuomotor coordination + planning. Knocking the stack down is also part of the practice.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/15-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/stacks-two-objects/complete
